styleAnswer.evidence: The outline passes. The edge pixels are 0% near-neutral and lean dark blue-grey beside the roof and dark green beside the sign, so they are tinted material tones rather than a black sticker line. The building is also a whole building like the references. The shading and texture fall short of the Beodeul standard. The cream clapboard wall is about 3 tones with line grain only, and the green sign band and the awning are mostly clean flat colour. The references carry speckled plaster, scalloped tiles with per-tile highlights and stones shaded one by one. The measured facts are 9 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 for the references, and 5% near-flat coverage against 0%. Both are close but slightly worse than the references. The candidate looks cleaner and more vector-like than the references, so I am failing it on the doubt rule.

The tile rows are the top surface, and a light eave edge line sits near row 66 with a dark eave below it. Below the roof is a tall vertical south face from row 68 to 159, made of the wall with windows, the sign, the awning and the shop front. The striped awning at rows 122-131 is a second sloped plane. The roof is split into a light left plane and a dark right plane at a central ridge, but no receding side wall is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a clean, readable shopfront, but it is shallower than the references. The slate roof has only about 4 steps (light, mid, dark, and a ridge line) and no per-tile scallops or highlights, so it reads as large smooth planes. The references' roofs have warm tile highlights, speckle and many steps. The cream siding is just horizontal lines on about 3 tones, and the green sign board is a large flat fill apart from the lettering. Outlines are tinted dark blue-grey and green-grey (0% near-neutral edge pixels), so it is not a sticker outline, which is a point in its favour. Measured facts: 9 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 for the references, and 5% near-flat coverage against 0%, so it is somewhat lower in density and has some flat areas. The awning stripes and produce shelf add detail at the bottom, but the upper two-thirds of the building lack the grain and clumped texture of the references. Not accepted next to Beodeul without looking flatter.
